title: Beatrix and the Protocol
premise: Cyrus Ashgrove has spent eleven years alone tending the Halcyon Seed Vault and its mysterious beacon, until a distress signal arrives in a language that died with the Meridian Compact two centuries ago. The message reveals the beacon is actually a countdown trigger for a fleet-wide weapons protocol, and the truce keeping three warring fleets at bay expires in forty days. Cyrus joins forces with Sefa, a defector archivist who can read the dead language, and the ragged crew of the courier Vantablack to reach the relay at the edge of dead space and silence the trigger. Betrayed by their own captain, who wants to sell the protocol to the highest bidder, Cyrus must choose between broadcasting the truth that will shatter the fragile peace and destroying the relay at the cost of the vault's living archive. In the end, Cyrus sacrifices the beacon and the vault's data core, exposing the protocol and forcing the fleets into an uneasy, honest negotiation—while Sefa and the crew become the family Cyrus never believed they deserved.
about_author: Vesper Ishikawa is a former radio astronomer who left observatory life to write about the people history forgets to remember. They live on a decommissioned listening station off the coast of Hokkaido, where they repair antique transmitters and insist the static is trying to say something.

chapters.title: The Keeper of Small Hours
chapters.summary: Cyrus Ashgrove's POV. We meet Cyrus in the quiet rhythm of vault maintenance—cataloguing seeds, winding the beacon, talking to the plants. A routine diagnostic reveals the beacon transmitting on a frequency no human system uses. Emotional beat: loneliness mistaken for peace, cracked open by the first anomaly in eleven years.

chapters.title: A Language of Ash
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The signal resolves into structured language—Meridian, dead for two centuries. Cyrus's desperate searches of the vault's decaying archives yield only fragments and one name: the Protocol of Halcyon. Emotional beat: the vertigo of realizing your quiet life was built on someone else's secret.

chapters.title: The Defector
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa, an archivist exiled for translating forbidden Meridian texts, intercepts the beacon's echo and realizes what it means: the beacon is a trigger for a dormant weapons protocol holding the fleet truce together. She charters the courier Vantablack to find the signal's source. Emotional beat: hope sharpened into obsession.

chapters.title: Strangers at the Airlock
chapters.summary: Alternating Cyrus and Sefa POVs. Sefa's crew arrives at the vault; Cyrus meets them armed with a maintenance laser and eleven years of paranoia. Distrust thaws over shared translation work as the signal's countdown becomes clear—forty days until the truce expires. Emotional beat: two lonely people recognizing each other.

chapters.title: What the Vault Was For
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Decoded fully, the signal reveals the vault was never a seed bank—it's the protocol's anchor, and the beacon a dead-man's switch. The fleet that abandoned Earth expects it to fire. Captain Oduya of the Vantablack grows strangely interested in the relay's coordinates. Emotional beat: the sickening discovery that Cyrus's sanctuary was a weapon all along.

chapters.title: Dead Space
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The Vantablack jumps for the relay, leaving the vault dark for the first time in Cyrus's life. In transit, the crew bonds—card games, Sefa teaching Cyrus Meridian, the engineer Rell's ghost stories. Emotional beat: found family forming in the cramped dark, and Cyrus grieving a home they can't return to.

chapters.title: The Price of the Truth
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. At dead space's edge, the relay looms—ancient, half-derelict, guarded by an automated Meridian defense grid. Oduya reveals her plan: sell the protocol to the Kessari fleet and retire rich. She maroons Sefa and Cyrus on the relay's outer hull. Emotional beat: loyalty curdling into betrayal; trust weaponized.

chapters.title: Countdown
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Trapped on the relay with the truce hours from expiring, Cyrus and Sefa fight through the grid using the vault's maintenance codes—Cyrus's years of invisible labor becoming the key. Rell, secretly loyal to them, sabotages Oduya and opens a docking ring. Emotional beat: the quiet competence of the overlooked becoming heroic.

chapters.title: The Protocol of Halcyon
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs, climax. At the relay's core, Cyrus faces the choice: broadcast the protocol's truth and shatter the truce with honesty, or destroy the relay—and the vault's archive—with silence. Cyrus chooses truth, transmitting the full record of the fleets' original betrayal to every ship in range, then kills the beacon. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into resolve.

chapters.title: Seeds
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV, epilogue. The fleets, exposed, convene the first honest negotiation in two centuries. Oduya faces her crew's judgment; Rell takes the helm of the Vantablack. Cyrus, vault-less but not homeless, plants a seed garden aboard the courier with Sefa beside them. Emotional beat: grief and belonging braided together—an ending that is a beginning.
